grade.first_issue: No decisive defect. The parenthetical claim that h=lcm(m,n)>1 always is false (for example, m=n=2 gives h=1), but it is extraneous: the preceding case analysis already shows that g>1 in the first case and h=mn>1 in the coprime case. Thus the Rule C deletion test is satisfied.
grade.summary: The lexicographically decreasing potential (total prime-factor count, number of entries greater than 1) correctly proves finite termination and, together with preservation of at least one nonunit, yields exactly one final entry M>1. Primewise, the move sends exponent pairs to (min(x,y),|x-y|), preserving the gcd of all exponents. At a terminal board this invariant equals v_p(M), determining M uniquely from the initial board. Apart from one harmless false parenthetical, the proof is complete.
strengths: The potential-function calculation is correct and establishes termination for every sequence of choices.
The two cases gcd(m,n)>1 and gcd(m,n)=1 correctly give strict lexicographic descent.
The valuation transformation and preservation of the gcd of the complete exponent list are correctly identified.
The terminal reconstruction v_p(M)=gcd_i v_p(a_i) proves choice-independence.

errors.description: The statement that h=lcm(m,n)>1 always is false; h=lcm(m,n)/gcd(m,n) and can equal 1. Deleting this parenthetical leaves the argument complete because the preceding exhaustive case analysis already preserves a nonunit.
